fields.what: Non-Abelian topological order (quantum double models): anyon braiding and fusion — layer 7, alternate on ion_qccd and sc, status E, since 2023

items.note: four independent groups with hardware (Quantinuum/Harvard on H2: D4 2024, Z3 2025, S3 with a universal gate set 2026 — Nature 655, 591; Google 2023; Zhejiang/Tsinghua 2024; IBM 2025); no demonstration is error-corrected, so status E; since = Google's Ising anyons (Nature 618, 264, May 2023). The brief; four dated records; requires cx_qccd | cx_nn | cx_lr (one of); alternative to code_surface.

fields.what: Resonator-induced phase gate on fluxonium (all-microwave) — layer 3, alternate on sc, status E, since 2026

items.note: one group on fluxonium (WMI/TUM, a preprint of 26 Aug 2026: five fluxoniums, connectivity four, 128 ns, refocused IRB 99.20(5)/98.4(1)/96.2(2)/99.44(3) %, median 98.8(12) %, ZZ < 1 kHz, GHZ5 90.0(2) %) — the editor's tier by the T2 review's own caveat; admitted as E on the standing instruction of 6 Nov 2026, his word pending; the undo is the N() entry, the slot, the edges and the brief. The gate's origin on IBM's 3D transmons (PRL 117, 250502, 2016) is cited as lineage. Closes the map gap G-rip in substance; the register row map-gaps.csv (resolved, resolution) is the register's and is not edited here.

fields.what: Frequency-division-multiplexed gate drive (several qubits per line) — layer 5, alternate on sc, status E, since 2026

items.note: one group (USTC/HNL/QuantumCTek, a preprint of 26 Oct 2026: a 1:4 demonstration — parallel FDM CZ (6.4 ± 0.2)e-3 vs (6.53 ± 0.24)e-3 dedicated, XY(π/2) (10.6 ± 0.2)e-4 vs (10.38 ± 0.35)e-4; filters at room temperature; 1/12 projected at the measured parameters, 1/48 idealised; 381,000 qubits on 23,814 lines) — the editor's tier by the T2 review's caveat; admitted as E on the standing instruction, his word pending. The BAQIS proposal of Dec 2023 (arXiv:2312.06911) is the lineage, grade S. The Tsinghua cryogenic multiplexing chip (arXiv:2610.19599) is a simulation whose arXiv record carries an inconsistent 2022 journal line; not cited.

fields.what: Dual-species ancilla readout (a second atomic species measured mid-circuit) — layer 6, alternate on atom_rb and atom_ae, status E, since 2023

items.note: two independent groups with hardware: U. Chicago (Bernien) — Rb–Cs platform PRX 12, 011040 (2022), Cs spectators read mid-circuit with feed-forward Science 380, 1265 (2023), interspecies CZ and QND readout of a Rb qubit through a Cs ancilla Nat. Phys. 20, 1744 (2024); Harvard (Ni) — Na ancilla reads the Z stabiliser of four-Cs plaquettes, 0.82(3) per data qubit (preprint, May 2026). The T2 candidate's second group, QudeLeap/HKUST(GZ) Rb–Yb CZ 99.91 % (arXiv:2609.11730), is a simulation (PairInteraction, quantum trajectories) — grade S, not hardware; the technology meets D3 on Chicago and Harvard. since = 2023 (the Science paper: the first mid-circuit readout of a second species as the ancilla); the T2 review said 2026.

fields.what: Cavity-based mid-circuit readout of tweezer atoms — layer 6, alternate on atom_rb and atom_ae, status E, since 2022

items.note: two independent groups: UC Berkeley (Stamper-Kurn) — one atom read in a cavity PRL 129, 203602 (2022); five Rb atoms, four measured mid-circuit at 0.9/0.2 % infidelity in 40 µs windows, 45 µs measurement-and-feed-forward cycle (preprint, Jun 2026); a Rydberg array in a cavity, 7.5 µs ground–Rydberg readout at 3/5 % (Oct 2026); Tsinghua/BAQIS (Chen) — 21 Rb atoms in a cooperativity-125 cavity, one-atom hyperfine readout 99.925 % in 4 µs, survival 99.996 % (Jul 2026). since = 2022 (the PRL: mid-circuit cavity measurement in a tweezer array, one atom); the T2 review said 2026. The readout's typical time -4.4 (40 µs) with the fast end -5.4 (4 µs, one atom) as the card's range.

fields.what: Cryogenic tweezer-array apparatus (blackbody suppression) — layer 10, alternate on atom_rb and atom_ae, status E, since 2021

items.note: four groups and one company: IOGS/Pasqal 6,000 s lifetimes (Phys. Rev. Appl. 16, 034013, 2021), 2,088 sites at 6 K (Phys. Rev. Appl. 22, 024073, 2024), 1,024 atoms defect-free at 4 K (PRX Quantum 7, 033032, 2026 — the record the report's bibliography already holds); JILA 3,000 s (PRX Quantum 6, 020337, 2025) and blackbody/avalanche suppression behind a 45 K shield (preprint, Nov 2026); MPQ 16 × 16 Sr with full optical access, > 7,000 s (preprint, Jul 2026; by its own account not a blackbody shield); Princeton's universal gate set in a cryogenic Cs array, CZ 99.76(8) % raw, 1Q 99.970(2) % (preprint, Oct 2026). since = 2021 (the first cryogenic tweezer array); the T2 review said 2026. Error structure loss + correlated bursts (the two it suppresses); place none — the shields are not control placement.

A5 of the review sheet, accepted by the editor on 7 Nov 2026: the median field holds medians, and the 22-qubit chain's average CZ error (4.35e-2, dominated by its worst pairs; best pair 1e-3) is not one. The text cell err_2q_median keeps the mean, the best pair and the parallel-CZ figures; the flag that qualified the number goes with it. Effect: the superconducting family's two-qubit-error median (§8.5, F2) returns from 4.7e-3 to 4.4e-3; the trapped-ion median 2.7e-3 (LYNX, a median over 276 pairs) stays. The row now states gate_evidence device-benchmark (the preprint's randomised benchmarking of the chain's pairs): a blank cell is derived from the numeric, and with the numeric blank the derivation would have read none and dropped the device from the benchmarked set of §8 — the figures are published, only the median is not.
